name: @mountainlift/cortex-mcp

tools.name: cortex_whoami
tools.description: Returns the currently authenticated Cortex Planner user (id, email, name, role) and the organisation the token reaches (tenant: id, slug, name). Use the id as the default userId for time-entry tools.

tools.name: cortex_time_entry_list
tools.description: Lists time entries with durations, task titles, Jira issue keys (task.jiraKey), project and client. Defaults to the current user. Use weekNumber+year for ISO weeks, or from/to dates. Running timers have endedAt=null and count elapsed time so far.

from.description: Entries starting from — ISO datetime or date-only YYYY-MM-DD (date-only is expanded to the whole local day)

to.description: Entries starting before — ISO datetime or date-only YYYY-MM-DD (date-only is expanded to the whole local day)

weekNumber.description: ISO week number; use together with year instead of from/to

userId.description: Filter by user; defaults to the current user. Other users require an admin/manager account.

isRunning.description: true = only running timers, false = only completed entries

tools.name: cortex_time_entry_create
tools.description: Creates a time entry. Omit endedAt to start a running timer (prefer cortex_timer_start for that). userId defaults to the current user; logging for others requires an admin/manager account.

startedAt.description: ISO datetime or date-only YYYY-MM-DD (date-only is expanded to the whole local day)

endedAt.description: ISO datetime or date-only YYYY-MM-DD (date-only is expanded to the whole local day)

taskId.description: Task to log against — find it with cortex_task_list

tools.name: cortex_time_entry_update
tools.description: Edits an existing time entry. Pass taskId: null to unassign the task. Only provided fields change.

startedAt.description: ISO datetime or date-only YYYY-MM-DD (date-only is expanded to the whole local day)

endedAt.description: ISO datetime or date-only YYYY-MM-DD (date-only is expanded to the whole local day)

tools.name: cortex_time_entry_delete
tools.description: Permanently deletes a time entry by id.

tools.name: cortex_timer_start
tools.description: Starts a running timer (a time entry with no end) for the current user. Never stops other running timers — multiple concurrent timers are supported; already-running ones are returned as otherRunning.

taskId.description: Task to track — find it with cortex_task_list

tools.name: cortex_timer_stop
tools.description: Stops a running timer (sets its end to now, or endedAt if given). With exactly one timer running, id can be omitted. With several running it lists them and asks for id — it never stops all of them implicitly.

tools.name: cortex_timer_current
tools.description: Lists the currently running timers with elapsed time. Defaults to the current user; other users require an admin/manager account.

tools.name: cortex_project_list
tools.description: Lists projects with their clients. Use project ids to filter time entries and tasks.

tools.name: cortex_client_list
tools.description: Lists clients. Requires an admin/manager account — developers get a permission error.

tools.name: cortex_task_list
tools.description: Searches tasks by title (case-insensitive) or filters by project. Jira-linked tasks include jiraKey (the Jira issue key, e.g. "EPC-123") — use it to map time entries to Jira issues.

tools.name: cortex_user_list
tools.description: Lists workspace users — find a userId for manager flows (logging or reading time for someone else).

tools.name: cortex_opportunity_list
tools.description: Lists the sales pipeline mirrored from Notion, each case with its budget, probability, expected close date and the capacity estimate delivery has put against it. Requires an admin/manager account — developers get a permission error. Estimate months are relative to the close date: 0 is the month it signs, 1 the month after.

tools.name: cortex_opportunity_forecast
tools.description: The pipeline added up by month: value and weighted forecast by the month a case is expected to close, and capacity needed by the month it would be worked — a different month. Also reports the team total capacity that month, which is a ceiling rather than free room: most of it is committed to running projects. Lost cases are excluded; cases with no close date are reported apart under `undated`. Admin/manager only.

tools.name: cortex_opportunity_estimate_set
tools.description: Replaces a case's whole capacity estimate, month for month. Send every month you want kept — an empty list clears the estimate. Months are relative to the expected close (0 = the month it signs), each month at most once, at most 59 months out. Admin/manager only.

monthOffset.description: 0 = the month the case closes, 1 = the month after

role.description: What profile is needed, as free text

estimates.description: The whole estimate. An empty array clears it.

tools.name: cortex_ticket_list
tools.description: Lists the tickets of Cortex's own backlog (the COR-N series), newest first: key, title, status and when it last changed. No descriptions — read a ticket in full with cortex_ticket_get. Filter by status: todo, in_progress or done. Admin/manager only.

tools.name: cortex_ticket_get
tools.description: Reads one ticket in full, description (markdown) included. `ref` is how people say it: COR-307, cor-307 or 307. Admin/manager only.

ref.description: The ticket: COR-307, the branch spelling cor-307, or 307

tools.name: cortex_ticket_create
tools.description: Files a new ticket; it gets the next number in the series. Status defaults to todo. The description is markdown. Admin/manager only.

tools.name: cortex_ticket_update
tools.description: Changes a ticket — only the fields you pass. This is how a ticket moves between todo, in_progress and done. A null description clears it; the title can be replaced but not cleared. Admin/manager only.

ref.description: The ticket: COR-307, the branch spelling cor-307, or 307
